data.title: Pull Request
data.tagline: Ask others to review and merge the work from one branch
data.description: A pull request is a collaboration feature on Git hosting platforms, not a core Git command. It collects the change summary, discussion, automated checks, and review before a branch is merged. Keep its scope focused and explain how the result was verified.

use: Keep a record of why a branch entered main
avoid: Open one request for several unrelated features
Use only the title and provide no context
Merge while required checks or questions remain unresolved
Treat review as permission to skip your own testing

explanation.title: Pull request vs merge request: is there a difference?
explanation.text: They name the same general review-before-merge workflow. GitHub, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps use Pull Request (PR); GitLab uses Merge Request (MR). Product features still differ. Core concept: Pull Request (PR) — A proposal to review branch changes and discuss code diffs before merging into a target branch.; Merge Request (MR) — GitLab's term for proposing, reviewing, and merging changes into a target branch.. Primary platform: Pull Request (PR) — Standard terminology on GitHub, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps.; Merge Request (MR) — Standard terminology on GitLab and GitLab CE/EE.. Product details: Pull Request (PR) — Review rules, checks, and merge options depend on the hosting product and repository settings.; Merge Request (MR) — Review rules, pipelines, and merge options depend on GitLab's edition and project settings.. Switching between GitHub and GitLab: On GitHub, a team opens a Pull Request; on GitLab, it opens a Merge Request. Both usually involve reviewing diffs, discussing changes, running checks, and approving a merge, but the available controls and rules depend on the platform and repository settings.

lessonPractice.title: A feature branch has a pull request with passing checks, but review finds that a button is clipped on mobile. What should happen next?

options.label: Merge because checks passed and fix mobile later on main
options.feedback: The checks did not cover this mobile defect. A known issue should not enter the main line because the status is green.

options.label: Fix it on the same branch, verify again, and review the pull request's latest changes
options.feedback: The pull request should collect the current code, discussion, and verification before the merge decision.

options.label: Close the pull request, copy the same code to main, and fix mobile there
options.feedback: Copying directly bypasses the discussion and change history. The feature branch should contain the reviewed final fix.

data.agentPrompt: Checks pass, but a mobile button is clipped. Fix it on the same branch, recheck mobile and desktop, and update the pull request summary and verification. Confirm the latest diff contains only this feature before requesting review, and do not bypass the PR by editing main.
